title: Pack three tools into their drawers (Franka, operational-space control)
text:
A black high-gloss chest of drawers (~37 cm wide, 36 cm tall) stands on the table: four sliding drawers stacked top to bottom, each with a real pull handle on its front. All drawers start shut. In front of the chest lie three tools: a green stapler, a pair of scissors, and a utility knife.
Goal: pull drawers open as needed and pack the tools — the STAPLER goes in the TOP (1st) drawer, the SCISSORS in the SECOND drawer, the KNIFE in the THIRD drawer (the 4th/bottom drawer stays shut and gets nothing) — then push every drawer shut. An item counts only inside its own drawer's tray; the job is done when all three tools are stowed and every drawer is shut.
success: Success, exactly: a fixed point of the green stapler's body, not necessarily its centre [its rigid-body origin], lies inside the top drawer's tray interior, the scissors' inside the second drawer's, and the utility knife's inside the third drawer's — each tray interior being a box measured in that drawer's own frame (so it moves with the drawer), 355 mm side-to-side x 139 mm front-to-back x 54 mm tall [tray_center (0, 0.0006, 0.0388) m +/- tray_half (0.1775, 0.0694, 0.0268) m in the drawer link frame]; all four drawers (including the empty bottom one) are pulled out less than 15 mm from fully shut; every tool moves slower than 0.05 m/s and every drawer slides slower than 0.05 m/s. Not true at the start (drawers shut, tools on the table).
